references.title: The lag draws the direction.

references.evidence: Kinetic model + fitted snapshot data
references.look: Read the RNA-processing chain, then trace the two arms of the unspliced–spliced phase portrait.
references.mechanism: Unspliced and spliced RNA respond with a lag as a gene switches on and off.
references.construction: Plot the two molecular quantities against each other. Fit an oriented trajectory through their joint states.
references.eye: The same spliced abundance can sit on different arms: rising and falling states need not look alike.
references.stronger: One expression curve or cluster map hides the ambiguity. The phase portrait makes the missing direction geometric.
references.borrow: When two quantities lag each other, pair them as coordinates; check whether direction or hysteresis becomes visible.
references.limit: This is model-based reconstruction from snapshots, not a movie of the same cells. Kinetic assumptions matter.

transfer.keep: Keep the axes physically defined. Distinguish observed points from fitted trajectory and inferred time.
build: Plot the paired state variables rather than each separately against an arbitrary index.
